inherits.scope: The HD63701V0 manual documents the same Hitachi timer and interrupt architecture; this profile states its distinct EPROM/RAM map, register reset facts, GPIO reset behavior, SCI framing rule, and operating modes locally.
restrictions: The wrapper implements every documented MCU operating mode: 0, 1, 2, 5, 6, and 7; Modes 3 and 4 are marked not used by the manufacturer.
The EPROM image and digital PROM program request use integration-owned storage; programming voltage, pulse, erasure, and retention physics are not represented.

Section 3.1 prose prints PROM addresses 0000 through 00FF, while the same sentence specifies 4 KiB and figure 3-3 maps 0000 through 0FFF; the implementation follows the internally consistent 4-KiB/0FFF boundary and records the prose range as a documentation discrepancy.
The contradictory Mode-5/7 address-error statements for 0040-007F remain undefined by documentation.
Nanosecond oscillator restart and electrical behavior remain outside the digital standby claim; CC1:CC0=00 is documented as an unavailable SCI selection.

gpio.port1: eight GPIO pins except in Mode 1, where they drive A0-A7
gpio.port2: five GPIO pins with timer and SCI overrides; P21 is input or timer output only
gpio.port3: eight Mode-7 GPIO pins with DDR, optional IS3 input latch, read- or write-selected OS3 pulse, and IS3 interrupt flag; external address/data bus in expanded modes
gpio.port4: eight GPIO pins in Modes 5/6/7 and a mode-selected address function in Modes 0/1/2
gpio.reset: all DDRs are asynchronously cleared while RES is low so pins enter the input state before synchronous internal reset release

sci.framing_error: a missing stop bit sets ORFE, leaves RDRF clear, and transfers the receive shift-register byte into RDR
sci.implemented_clock_modes: internally clocked NRZ with divisors 16, 128, 1024, and 4096, plus external NRZ divided from eight sampled P22 positive edges per bit
sci.reserved_clock_modes: CC1:CC0=00 has no format or clock source; the wrapper disables the Motorola-only bi-phase engine

operating_modes.mode0: multiplexed manufacturer test mode with internal F000-FFFF EPROM except the initial external reset-vector fetch; implemented digitally
operating_modes.mode1: expanded non-multiplexed 64-KiB operation with internal EPROM disabled and Ports 1/3/4 carrying address/data; implemented at the normalized boundary
operating_modes.mode2: expanded multiplexed operation with internal EPROM disabled; implemented at the normalized boundary
operating_modes.mode5: non-multiplexed partial decode with internal EPROM and external 0100-01FF; implemented at the normalized boundary
operating_modes.mode6: multiplexed partial decode with internal EPROM; implemented at the normalized boundary
operating_modes.mode7: single-chip operation with 192-byte RAM and internal F000-FFFF EPROM; implemented
operating_modes.prom_programming: digital 27256-compatible PROM mode with MCU functions stopped: Port 1 and Port 4/IRQ form A14:A0, Port 3 carries D7:D0, P46 is active-low OE, P47 is active-low CE, PROM 0000-0FFF maps to MCU F000-FFFF, 1000-7FFF reads erased FF, and table 3-1 read/output-disable/program/verify/inhibit states are implemented; analog voltage, pulse, erase, and retention behavior is excluded
operating_modes.unavailable: Modes 3 and 4 are marked not used
operating_modes.sleep: SLP stops CPU execution while peripherals continue; implemented by the shared HD6301 CPU profile
operating_modes.standby: standby_n_i asynchronously enters reset state, suppresses program/GPIO activity, preserves RAM and supplied STBY_PWR, and restarts through the reset vector on release

reference.locator: sections 2.1, 2.12, and 3.1, printed pages 252-262 and 287-294

memory_control.RAME: bit 6 resets set and enables physical 0040-00FF RAM in every legal mode; clearing it exposes the selected mode's documented external or unusable behavior
memory_control.STBY_PWR: read/write retained-supply validity bit initialized deterministically on external reset, preserved through STBY while standby_power_ok_i is true, and cleared when it is false
memory_control.address_trap: Modes 0/1/2/6 trap fetches at 0000-001F; Mode 5 traps 0000-003F and 0200-EFFF; Mode 7 traps 0000-003F and 0100-EFFF. The table's conflicting inclusion of physical RAM at 0040-007F in Modes 5/7 is explicitly unverified.
memory_control.eprom: F000-FFFF is read-only internal EPROM in Modes 0/5/6/7 and external in Modes 1/2; Mode-0 reset vectors initially come from external memory

reference.locator: memory maps, sections 2.11, 2.13, and 3.1, printed pages 259-262 and 286-294

implementation_scope.rtl: rtl/hd6301/hd63701v0_mcu.sv implements every legal Mode-0/1/2/5/6/7 memory and peripheral selection; hd63701v0_bus_wrapper.sv adds four-subphase Port-1/2/3/4, AS/IOS, R/W/OS3, reset, low-power, and standby pins
implementation_scope.model: model/hd63701v0_device.py independently selects every legal device mode, model/hd63701v0_bus.py independently projects physical digital pin phases, and model/hd63701v0_prom.py independently classifies the 27256-compatible PROM interface
implementation_scope.verification: A 95-check decode suite, 30-check six-core execution bench, Mode-7 directed/model suites, 468-check all-mode physical wrapper bench, and 28-check PROM bench cover memory, TRAP, peripheral, reset, standby, WAI/SLP, address/data, AS/IOS, R/W/OS3, GPIO, and every documented table-3-1 PROM state; the pin model exhaustively projects 65,536 active addresses and the PROM model exhaustively checks all 32,768 PROM addresses
implementation_scope.excluded_modes: Modes 3 and 4 are not used; PROM voltage magnitude, programming-pulse timing, erasure, charge retention, nanosecond timing, pads, and oscillator recovery delay remain unclaimed
analog_exclusions: PROM programming voltage magnitude and pulse timing
